similarityMetric: 5-word shingle Jaccard, the metric scripts/check-programmatic-uniqueness.mjs already applies to the 78 compatibility pages

reasoning.originalWordFloor: Measured minimum across the 20 pilot pages is 315 original words, excluding every shared boilerplate string. A 250-word floor sits about 20% under that minimum: ordinary variation in a future person cannot trip it, while a genuinely thin page — one where the chart offered little to say — fails closed. For scale, the site's own daily readings run 90–140 words and weekly 200–300.
reasoning.substantiveStatementFloor: Measured minimum is 11 distinct substantive statements. A floor of 8 leaves headroom for a chart with fewer aspects inside orb and no dignities at all, which is the sparsest case the pilot's own screening produced.
reasoning.similarityCeiling: Measured maximum pairwise similarity is 0.2786 (rosalind-franklin <> katherine-johnson). A 0.32 ceiling sits about 15% above that, and well under the 0.42 the repository already accepts for the more formulaic compatibility pairs.
reasoning.excludedFromOriginalCount: Shared strings — the data-quality note, the evidence-disclosure labels, navigation, cross-link labels and the portrait credit — are boilerplate by design and are not counted as original copy. Counting them would let a page pass on chrome.

sectExclusionNote: Sect (day/night chart) is time-dependent: it asks whether the Sun was above the horizon. On an unknown-time record the noon convention would always answer 'day chart', which is an artefact of the assumption rather than a fact about the person. Sect is therefore excluded from the substantive-statement set for unknown-time records, alongside rising sign, houses and angles, and is available only where a real birth time is sourced.
